newsitem.title: INDONESIA: OPINION-Small Indonesian banks offer opportunities.
newsitem.headline: OPINION-Small Indonesian banks offer opportunities.

text.p: JAKARTA, Aug 1 - There has been considerable interest in Indonesia's banking sector with the government's policy of encouraging mergers and acquisitions in order to improve the efficency of the sector as a prelude to opening it up for foreign competition and to reduce systemic risk.

Of particular interest now are some of the medium and smaller sized banks. The recent moves, including Bank Niaga's major shareholding changes, are indications of the shifts that are likely to take place over the next twelve months.
The sector is likely to be subject to much corporate activity. Many banks have already established task forces to identify suitable acquisition targets.

PE valuations of Indonesian banking stocks are strongly driven by stock liquidity with the more liquid banks (i.e. BNI, BII, BDNI, Lippo ) commanding significant premia over the stocks of less liquid peers. Mergers and acquisitions will necessarily improve stock liquidity which in turn should result in PE revaluations, which would be more significant for the smaller banks.

Corporate restructurings follow the deregulation of the Indonesian banking industry, most notably the change in capital adequacy, which was announced in 1995. Commercial banks' CAR (capital adequacy ratio) and minimum paid-up capital will be raised in stages from the current eight percent to 12 percent and from 10 billion rupiah to 150 billion rupiah, respectively. These new levels significantly increase the cost of participation in the industry.

Other important regulations put a cap on intra-group lending, which is now restricted to 10 percent of capital, which makes it less worthwhile for Indonesian conglomerates to associate closely with a commercial bank. As banks step away from the shelters of business groups, they need to diversify their business to have the same synergies from cross-selling of products as their international peers.

Bank stocks in general have performed well over the past 12 months before taking a dip last month due to currency concerns. Although in the short-term there may still be some weakness, we would expect the smaller banks (especially those involved in mergers and acquisitions) to outperform in the medium-term. Of special interest among these would be:

The recent change in the major shareholder from Julius Tahija's family to Hashim Djojohadikusumo should produce a rapid increase in the bank's size, while the stock split and bonus shares may improve liquidity.

The shares have already performed exceptionally well after the announcement of it being sold to Mr. Djojohadikusumo. Next year's earnings target is going to be boosted because, according to the management, by the end of 1997 all the bad debts stemming from Niaga's early ventures into auto financing will be written off.

Niaga's tie-up with the Rashid Hussain group of Malaysia will enable Niaga to compete successfully in the merchant banking market, which is becoming increasingly important. A smaller bank, Bank Papan Sejahtera, is also part of Mr. Djojohadikusumo's business empire. There should be synergies between Papan's mortgage lending and Niaga's corporate focus.

Despite an already high CAR (16 percent), the bank recently concluded a 361 billion rupiah rights issue. The bank plans to acquire a smaller bank and a multi-finance company and intends to increase its shareholdings in existing subsidiaries (e.g. Bank PDFCI ) to 20 percent of their paid-up capital in order to be able to equity account for them. The rights issue may also improve liquidity.

The bank has a focused strategy, lending to small to medium scale customers in Jakarta. The deposit gathering scheme "Tiara Mas," which targets the upper end of the middle class, appears to be very successful, while the aggressively-marketed high-tech banking approach seems to be highly attractive for the target group. We expect Bank Tiara to become the trend-setter in loan syndications for the middle market and anticipate further strong profit growth.
(NOTE-The views expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as reflecting the views of Reuters).
